skill.name: deslop
skill.description: Remove AI-generated code slop from a branch. Use when cleaning up AI-generated code, removing unnecessary comments, defensive checks, or type casts. Checks diff against main and fixes style inconsistencies.
skill.summary: Prompt-only cleanup guide for reviewing branch diffs and removing AI-generated code artifacts.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The two static findings are false positives caused by markdown inline code, not executable Ruby or shell syntax. The skill is prompt-only and the only command is a hardcoded read-only git diff. One semantic concern remains: the guidance could encourage removal of defensive checks without enough safety boundaries.

remediation.suggestion: Clarify that validation, authorization, error handling, and boundary checks must be preserved unless tests and domain context prove them redundant.

static_findings.snippet: - Casts to `any` to get around type issues
1. Get the diff against main: `git diff main...HEAD`

finding_verdicts.reason: The text is markdown inline code around the type name any, not shell backtick execution. It does not instruct running a command or executing user-controlled input.
The line shows a hardcoded git diff command for local review. It is read-only and has no user-controlled interpolation, network use, or credential access.

semantic_findings.title: Risky Guidance to Remove Defensive Checks
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs users to remove defensive checks or try/catch blocks that seem abnormal. Without explicit safeguards, this could lead an agent to remove validation or error handling that protects security boundaries.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Line 13 directly instructs removal of defensive checks and try/catch blocks. The wording limits this to abnormal codepaths, but it lacks a warning to preserve authorization, validation, and boundary checks.

content.value_statement: AI-assisted branches can accumulate comments, defensive wrappers, and style drift. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through targeted diff cleanup.
actual_capabilities: Reviews branch changes against the main branch diff.
Identifies excessive comments that do not match nearby code style.
Flags unnecessary defensive wrappers and unusual try/catch usage.
Finds type casts used to bypass type issues.
Encourages moving inline Python imports to standard import locations.
Summarizes cleanup changes in one to three sentences.
limitations: It does not run tests or prove that removed code is safe.
It depends on the current branch having a comparable main branch.
It may need human judgment for validation and error handling changes.
It does not replace a full code review.

use_cases.title: Review AI-assisted pull requests
use_cases.description: Clean up noisy comments, defensive wrappers, and style drift before requesting review.

use_cases.title: Prepare branch diffs for maintainers
use_cases.description: Reduce unrelated cleanup noise so maintainers can focus on the intended code change.

use_cases.title: Standardize generated changes
use_cases.description: Bring generated code closer to local style before merging into a shared repository.

prompt_templates.title: Basic branch cleanup
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this after AI-assisted implementation work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my branch against main with the deslop skill. Remove clear AI-generated cleanup noise and summarize the changes.

prompt_templates.title: Comment cleanup review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when generated comments feel excessive.
prompt_templates.prompt: Focus on comments added in this branch. Remove comments that are obvious, redundant, or inconsistent with the surrounding files.

prompt_templates.title: Defensive code audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when defensive wrappers may be unnecessary.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review defensive checks and try/catch blocks in the branch. Preserve validation, authorization, and boundary checks unless the codebase clearly proves they are redundant.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced style pass
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this before final review on a larger generated branch.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare changed files with nearby patterns. Remove AI-generated style drift, unnecessary casts, misplaced imports, and cleanup noise while preserving behavior.

output_examples.input: Review a branch that added verbose comments and extra wrappers around trusted internal helpers.
output_examples.output: Removed redundant explanatory comments and simplified unnecessary wrappers around existing trusted calls. Preserved input validation at module boundaries.

output_examples.input: Clean a TypeScript change that used broad casts to bypass type errors.
output_examples.output: Replaced unsafe broad casts with clearer typed values where the surrounding code supported it. Left unresolved type design questions for review.

output_examples.input: Prepare a Python branch with inline imports added by generated code.
output_examples.output: Moved inline imports to the file import section and aligned the changed file with existing import order. No behavior changes were introduced.

best_practices: Run tests after any cleanup that changes control flow or error handling.
Preserve security checks, validation, authorization, and boundary protections.
Review the final diff manually before merging.
anti_patterns: Do not remove defensive code only because it looks generated.
Do not hide real type problems with broader casts.
Do not use this as a substitute for product or security review.

faq.question: What does this skill help remove?
faq.answer: It targets AI-generated cleanup noise such as redundant comments, unusual defensive wrappers, broad casts, and inconsistent style.

faq.question: Does it change code automatically?
faq.answer: It guides an AI agent through a cleanup review. The agent may edit files when used in an editing environment.

faq.question: Is the git diff command required?
faq.answer: The process uses a branch diff against main to find new changes. Equivalent review context can also work.

faq.question: Can it remove security checks?
faq.answer: It should not remove validation, authorization, or boundary checks without clear evidence and human review.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Should I run tests after using it?
faq.answer: Yes. Run relevant tests after cleanup, especially when edits affect control flow, errors, or types.
